observations: Photo 0 shows a person in a grey work uniform with 'FABRIT' on the chest, standing on a pile of car engines in a warehouse.
Photo 1 and Photo 2 show a single engine assembly wrapped in plastic film.
The engine has a black plastic cover on the top, which is typical for a 4-cylinder engine.
The engine is mounted on a transmission housing, suggesting it is a 4-cylinder engine with a 5-speed automatic transmission.
The engine is marked with 'C5N' in white paint on the black cover in photo 1.
The engine appears to be used, with some surface rust and wear visible on the plastic wrap and engine components.

claims.evidence: Only one engine is shown in photos 1 and 2; the seller cannot confirm the presence of other brands or gearboxes.

risks.risk: The engine may not be a 4-cylinder as the 'C5N' marking suggests a 4-cylinder engine with a 5-speed automatic transmission.
risks.proof: A photo of the engine code plate (usually on the engine block or the transmission cover).
risks.if_unproven: as a 4-cylinder engine with a 5-speed automatic transmission

risks.risk: The engine may be a used part from a different vehicle than the seller claims.
risks.proof: A photo of the engine code plate showing the VIN or the specific vehicle model.

risks.risk: The engine may be missing the necessary accessories like the alternator, battery, or air filter.
risks.proof: A photo showing all the engine components and accessories.
risks.if_unproven: as a bare engine without accessories

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the engine code plate (usually on the engine block or the transmission cover).
Photo showing the engine with all accessories (alternator, battery, air filter).
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
